card.name: Risk wording in warning sentences
card.fires_on: The word right after a risk or caution phrase in label warnings, such as "death" after "risk of" or "to" after "it is reasonable". Also the word after an "If ... effects are seen," clause.

modes.label: Death after risk of
modes.description: The word "death" completing "risk of" in mortality warnings.
modes.example: Antipsychotic drugs increase the all-cause risk of<< death>> in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis.

modes.label: Reasonable to expect
modes.description: The word "to" after "it is reasonable" before "expect similar risk".
modes.example: Because of similar pharmacological properties, it is reasonable<< to>> expect similar risk with the concomitant

modes.label: Conditional advice clause
modes.description: A linking word inside a conditional sentence about what to do if effects appear.
modes.example: If anticholinergic effects are seen,<< the>> dose of procyclidine should be reduced

card.writes: Output effects are unclear; the suppressed tokens are Chinese hedging phrases such as "not necessarily", so it may weakly discourage hedged continuations.
card.plain: It fires on the key word in warning sentences about risk, especially death, and on phrases like "it is reasonable to expect".
